questions.question: Narrate the case with suitable Title for the case. Justify your title.
questions.solution_html:
• Narrate the case with suitable Title for the case. Justify your title
  • **Title - “The Hidden Inequality Behind Employee Equality” (2marks)
  • Narration: (5marks)
  • Watson Public Limited Company, known for its fair treatment of employees and strong
  • employee–management relations, faced sudden issues in quality, mismatch in packing
  • materials, incorrect labelling of material, not despatching the material on time etc. Des pite a
  • strong culture of equality symbolized through identical uniforms and shared benefits,
  • discontent started to grow.
  • Upon investigation, it was found that the company had hired new employees for higher-level
  • posts without considering internal candidates. These new recruits were also offered higher
  • pay packages compared to existing employees in the same cadre. This created dissatisfaction,
  • lowered morale, and resulted in negligence and errors in work.
  • Justification of the Title: (3marks)
  • The title “The Hidden Inequality Behind Employee Equality” reflects how the company’s
  • visible equality was contradicted by unfair internal practices like unequal pay and
  • overlooked promotions. Though the company preached equality, hidden disparities
  • damaged employee motivation and organisational harmony.

questions.final_answer: damaged employee motivation and organisational harmony.

questions.question: Help the organization to come out from this critical issue. If you are in the role of HR manager what will be your immediate step to solve this case.
questions.solution_html:
• Help the organisation to come out from this critical issue. If you are in the role of HR
  • Manager what will be your immediate step to solve this case.
  • Immediate Steps as HR Manager: (10marks)
  • Conduct an Employee Satisfaction Survey:
  • Collect honest feedback to understand the extent of dissatisfaction and specific
  • grievances among existing employees.
  • Review Compensation and Promotion Policies:
  • Ensure pay parity and transparent promotion criteria. Internal employees with
  • experience and performance should get fair consideration for promotions before
  • hiring externally.
  • Communicate Transparently:
  • Arrange an open meeting to explain the reasons behind external recruitment and
  • assure employees that fairness will be restored through structured HR policies.
  • Develop an Internal Career Growth Plan:
  • Introduce a system of internal job postings and skill development programs so that
  • deserving employees can grow within the company.
  • Recognition and Reward Programmes:
  • Reinforce motivation by recognizing the contributions of long-term employees
  • through performance-based incentives and awards.
  • Long-Term HR Strategy:
  • Build a balanced compensation structure and establish clear career paths, ensuring
  • both fairness and competitiveness in the job market.
  • **Each student is free to propose title for the case study and take immediate steps to solve the case.

questions.question: a. Case Study 1: Unilever's Global Virtual Team for Sustainable Innovation Background: Unilever, a global FMCG giant, has committed to achieving sustainability goals by 2030. To drive this initiative, the company formed a virtual innovation team consisting of employees from its R&D, marketing, and supply chain departments across the UK, India, Brazil, and the Netherlands. The team was tasked with designing eco-friendly packaging solutions. The team collaborated using platforms like Microsoft Teams, Trello, and cloud-based simulation tools. Members worked asynchronously due to time zone differences. Although the project progressed well, some issues emerged—cultural misunderstandings, uneven participation, and a lack of emotional connection among team members. The Turning Point: To address the issues, Unilever introduced structured "virtual bonding" sessions, digital brainstorming rooms, and a rotation system for team leads. With clear guidelines and regular feedback loops, the virtual team succeeded in developing a biodegradable packaging model within nine months—now implemented in over 30 countries.
